hypothesis: Deterministic detection of wasted slots (filler phrases + Jaccard near-dupes) on the exp011 draft, then refilling only those slots with a scoped model call, should recover coverage without needing a ranking judgment — because the 3B often knows task-specific unknowns but wastes slots on redundant/vague questions.
technique: A deterministic Swift pass identifies wasted slots on the exp011 contrastive-RAG draft using curated filler-phrase patterns and content-word Jaccard near-dupe detection; a single scoped model call then refills only those flagged slots (shown the kept set, no universal checklist, instructed to be specific); a defensive Swift re-check reverts any refills that are themselves filler or dupes, leaving strong slots verbatim.
result: Scored 0.282 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), down 0.041 from the exp011 best of 0.323 and 0.025 below the 0.307 baseline — discarded. NonRed held at 4 (the detector worked mechanically) but the refill step introduced new low-value/niche questions and fresh atomicity violations (atom=4, cover=3), confirming that deterministic detection can find the wasted slot but cannot tell the 3B what critical unknown should replace it — closing the detect-and-repair lever entirely.
